pr_title: fix animation blend tree update on inspector property input count change
pr_body:
Fixes #45437 and  #49375

Connects blend tree plugin to the `"tree_changed"` signal which is emited when input count is updated in the inspector. The signal then calls `_update_graph()` to refresh the blend tree graph.

Duplicate of #49404 
I did not realize that deleting the fork would cause me to be unable to edit the pull request after re-forking (I was not planning on contributing for a while). 

I was told I would have to make a new pull request. I apologize for any duplicated work on the maintainers.
pr_comments:
Oh, I understand. The reason why the drawing is not updated is because `AnimationNode` is just a resource and its parent, `AnimationBlendTree`, needs to do the redrawing.In other words, updating only the parameters of `AnimationNode` will not update the drawing.

However, `tree_changed` is still an exaggeration. If we subscribe to it, for example, it would be strange to have `tree_changed` fire when the number of inputs to `NodeTransition` goes up or down, so you should avoid it.

So, I think the correct way is to implement a "public function to update individual containers" or a "public function to redraw only dirty containers with dirty flag" in `AnimationBlendTree` and call it.

----
Another concern is that the relationship between the signal and the function may be opposite. Currently, _update_graph() can only be called from update_tree signal. Even if we don't update individual nodes, I think that _update_graph() should be renamed to update_tree() and make it a public function, and then the update_tree signal should be fired in that function.
cc @TokageItLab @SaracenOne Please assess whether this needs to be in 4.0 / in beta, thanks :)
It is not critical and does not need to be fixed before BETA, but it must be fixed before RC. We will need to discuss the right way for the fix with @reduz later.

issue_context.title: AnimationNodeTransition does not visually update upon changing input count or input names
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:**
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->
v3.2.3-stable


**OS/device including version:**
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->
Manjaro Linux, running kernel `5.9.1-1-rt19-MANJARO` (64-bit), using KDE with Plasma version `5.20.4` in X11.

Using an Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060 6GB with driver version 455.45.01.

Performed in 2D mode, using GLES3.


**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
Upon updating an Transition node's "Input Count" property or any input of the Transition node's "Name" property within an AnimationNodeBlendTree will not visually update the number of inputs or the names of the inputs until another node is added to the AnimationNodeBlendTree. 

Closing the editor (that is, quitting to the project list or closing the program entirely) and reopening the project also visually updates the Transition node. Closing the scene and reopening it does not update the Transition node.

Deleting the node and then undoing the action will also update the Transition node.

Deleting the parent AnimationTree and then undoing the action does not update the Transition node.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Within an AnimationNodeBlendTree, place a Transition node.
2. Update the "Input Count" parameter and/or the "Name" parameter of any input of the Transition node.
3. Place any other node within the AnimationNodeBlendTree to update the Transition node, OR close and reopen the project in its entirety, OR delete the Transition node and undo the action.


**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
[example.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5864192/example.zip)
comments: This is probably due to a missed `_change_notify()` method call in one of the setters or inspector tools.
I would like to try and implement the fix.

@Cartogy Sure, go ahead :slightly_smiling_face: 

Look for instances of `_change_notify(` in the codebase. This will help you understand how it should be used.

This issue is not only for AnimationNodeTransition but for others such as AnimationNodeAnimation.
I tried using *_change_notify("input_count")* in **AnimationNodeTransition::set_enabled_inputs(...)** as a solution but that did not work.

In **AnimationNodeAnimation::set_animation** there is a *_change_notify("animation")* called but the field is not updated until you add another node. Just like what happens with the AnimationNodeTransition.

I've been trying to see how the tree gets updated once adding a new node, but so far I don't know how the tree actually updates the nodes inside the blend tree. I looked into **AnimationNodeBlendTree::add_node** and commented out: *emit_changed()* and *emit_signal("tree_changed")* to see if this would stop updating the nodes in the editor, but it somehow still updates the nodes.

I also commented out *_change_notify()* in **AnimationTree::_update_properties**, but still the nodes in the editor change once adding a new node.

I may be missing something and need some help in figuring out how the blend nodes get updated when adding a new node.

Hey, Cartogy.  

It looks to me like AnimationNodeBlendTreeEditor::_update_graph() is the function that is being used to redraw the AnimationNodeBlendTree graph and update the data of the items displayed there.  

Typing text in the inspector fields triggers EditorInspector::_property_changed(), but doesn't trigger AnimationNodeBlendTreeEditor::_update_graph().

Thanks for helping, Cahlien!

After looking in toe AnimationNodeBlendTreeEditor::_update_graph, I'm starting to think the main issue is that the function _change_notify() for some reason is not registered when called in the AnimationNodeBlendTree. I could be wrong. I'll keep on investigating.

After debugging at bit more, I discovered that the _update_graph() does not update the blend tree editor. The blend tree editor shows the changes when the function **OS_X11::run()** is called. Specifically after  **3607: Main::iteration()** is called.

> The blend tree editor shows the changes when the function **OS_X11::run()** is called. Specifically after **3607: Main::iteration()** is called.

These are the two first steps of the backtrace, which don't help us isolate the source of this bug. You'll always see them when getting a backtrace anywhere in Godot.
Just realized that when dragging the node, the node's states in the blend tree does not update when **_update_graph()** is called. Only when adding a node.

I was wrong. The **AnimationNodeBlendTreeEditor::_update_graph** does update the nodes and shows its states.
The loop responsible is this specific one: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d7aea6ff6c54466dba51b75de5942154fbffe75d/editor/plugins/animation_blend_tree_editor_plugin.cpp#L149

I added **_change_notify("input_count")** based on the property's name: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/28e36dc7b99afe4adb8edfbd2a052ae5de303109/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp#L831 after *_update_inputs* in :https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/28e36dc7b99afe4adb8edfbd2a052ae5de303109/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp#L691 
and it does not update the blend tree. I noticed that **change_notify("animation")** for NodeAnimation  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/28e36dc7b99afe4adb8edfbd2a052ae5de303109/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp#L37 
also does not update the field in the blend tree.
recently I got this issue too when I using transition node, a bit of annoying, specially when you have a lot of this kind node, hope can be fixed

review_comments: The `tree_changed` is an exaggeration. It is a signal to use when the number of nodes in the tree increases or decreases, so you should fix it using available local functions such as `_validate_property()` instead.
